# gristmillr

gristmillr is an [httr2](https://httr2.r-lib.org/)-based client for the
[Grist](https://www.getgrist.com/) REST API. Functions take a lightweight
document handle first and return data frames, so they compose with pipes.

This is a development version; see `NEWS.md`.

## Setup

Set your API key (and, for a team or self-hosted site, the server) in
`.Renviron`:

```
GRIST_API_KEY=<your key>
GRIST_SERVER=https://myteam.getgrist.com
```

Or pass the key to `grist_doc(api_key = )`, as a string or as a function such
as `\() keyring::key_get("grist")`. Keys given as strings are never saved with
the object.

## Usage

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(gristmillr)

doc <- grist_doc("<doc id or URL>")
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
# The output below is computed against a scratch document that is deleted when
# the README is knitted.
devtools::load_all(quiet = TRUE)
workspace <- grist_workspaces()$id[[1]]
doc <- grist_doc_create(workspace, "gristmillr README")
grist_table_create(doc, "People", c(name = "Text", age = "Int", status = "Choice"))
grist_records_add(
  doc,
  "People",
  data.frame(
    name = c("Ann", "Bob", "Cy"),
    age = c(31L, 45L, 28L),
    status = c("active", "pending", "active")
  )
)
```

```{r}
grist_tables(doc)

doc |>
  grist_records("People", filter = list(status = "active"), sort = "-age")

doc |>
  grist_records_add("People", data.frame(name = "Dee", age = 52L, status = "active"))

grist_sql(doc, "SELECT status, COUNT(*) AS n FROM People GROUP BY status")
```

See `vignette("gristmillr")` to get started and `vignette("joining-tables")`
for working with reference columns.

## Coming from gristapi

The [gristapi](https://github.com/spyrales/gristapi) package is built around an R6 object. gristmillr has no stateful
objects: the document handle holds only an ID, a server and request settings,
and every function takes and returns data frames.

| gristapi         | gristmillr                                     |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------|
| `listtables()`   | `grist_tables()`                               |
| `listcolumns()`  | `grist_columns()`                              |
| `fetch_table()`  | `grist_records()`                              |
| `countrows()`    | `grist_count()`                                |
| `add_records()`  | `grist_records_add()`                          |
| `update_records()` | `grist_records_update()`                     |
| `delete_records()` | `grist_records_delete()`                     |
| `sync_table()`   | no equivalent yet (no upsert)                  |

Other differences:

* Cell types are converted from column metadata by default, with
  `convert = "basic"` and `"raw"` as alternatives.
* Settings that rarely change live in `grist_request_options()`,
  `grist_read_options()` and `grist_write_options()`.
* gristmillr also covers documents and workspaces, schema changes, SQL,
  downloads, attachments, webhooks and document history.
* It does not depend on dplyr, tidyr or sf.

```{r, include = FALSE}
grist_doc_delete(doc, mode = "permanent", confirm = TRUE)
```
